plans.objective: [DIM: structure] The solution space of small feedforward networks interpolating analytic constraints exhibits a phase transition in capacity N_c(w) at critical sample size w_c, where rigid (low-dimensional) behavior transitions to fat (high-dimensional) behavior as the constraint manifold becomes underdetermined.

steps.description: Implement the bootstrap experiment to verify zero-violation reachability using a linearly separable constraint family (rigid case). This constructs a minimal working example with w=3, width=16, seed=42, training steps=1000, learning_rate=1e-3, and validation threshold ≤1e-3. The script will output the anchor configuration (width, training violation, validation violation) to prove the experimental setup can achieve zero violation before proceeding to the full N_c(w) scan.

plans.objective: [DIM: structure] The phase transition in N_c(w) occurs at a critical constraint density w_c where the Hessian of the loss landscape changes rank from positive-definite to singular, indicating a bifurcation in the solution space geometry.

steps.description: Conduct a bootstrap numerical experiment to test the phase transition hypothesis in solution space rigidity. First, establish a zero-violation anchor using a low-dimensional linear constraint problem (w=3, width=16, seed=42) to confirm feasibility. Then, systematically vary constraint density w (5,10,15,20,30) and measure the minimum network width N_c(w) that achieves zero violation (≤1e-3) on held-out constraints, using 3 random seeds per w. Analyze the trend of N_c(w) against w to infer rigidity (decreasing/flat) vs. fatness (increasing), with Hessian rank change as the theoretical marker of the critical point w_c.
